items.note: 自然で正確。小道がpathに合う。
A/B/C/Eは正確。Dは誤字がある。
見た目と価格の両方を自然に表現。Aは不自然で誤り。
趣旨のメモが自然で正確。Dは給食が誤訳。
当初がoriginallyに最も自然に対応。Bは意味がずれる。
自然で丁寧、old ladyをおばあさんと適切に表現。
テストに落ちることがありますかが自然で意味も合う。
正確で丁寧。Bは句点欠けと『こう』がやや不自然。
身の危険を感じますが自然で、fear for my lifeの意味をよく表す。
give me a ringを自然な依頼として訳している。Bは待っているだけで依頼にならない。
自然と馴染むニュアンスが最もよく出ている。
among themの寄ってたかってという感じを自然に表現。
まだ決めかねていますがmake up my mind yetに自然で丁寧。
主語を省いて自然で正確。Aは表記と語順がやや不自然。
complainingを文句と訳して自然で口調も合う。Dはyourをきみたちにしている。
主語も含めて正確で自然。Bは継続の『ずっと』が弱い。
簡潔で自然、意味も正確。
音量を下げてくださいが最も正確で丁寧。
ばったり会いましたがcame acrossの偶然性を自然に表す。Dは英字表記が不適切。
収まるどころか、さらに激しくなったが正確で自然。
for goodを『もう戻ってきません』と自然に表現。永遠に去るは硬く不自然。
簡潔で自然、honest manを正直な人と適切に訳している。
悪い習慣がつくとなかなか抜けない、という定型的で自然な表現。
名前をカタカナにし、自然で正確。Dは文法的に破綻。
A-D准确自然；E更像secret passage，略窄。
各项都准确自然；A口语且贴合by train/left。
都准确；D最自然口语，价格也挺合适贴切。
A准确表达to the effect that且时态合适；B/D/E暗示已出去。
都准确自然；B补出这次会议更完整。
D自然准确；A食品杂货生硬，B杂货泛化，C省略her car。
B准确自然；D也好但稍正式，C“做到的考试”不自然。
各项均准确自然。
都准确；D简洁自然，贴合fear for my life。
都正确；A带“吧”语气更自然。
C/D准确表达不知不觉进入新生活；A偏融入，B偏适应。
B自然准确；C少了among them的合力感，D带贬义且不准。
都准确；C礼貌自然，拿定主意贴合。
A准确自然；B“很大的噪音”搭配稍别扭。
完全相同且准确自然。
各项准确；A最简洁自然。
C自然表达好运终会耗尽；A略生硬，D“把运气用完”稍怪。
都准确；B“调小一点”最自然礼貌。
E准确自然；D保留英文名且较混杂。
A准确自然；B较书面但好，C较口语粗略，D“猛烈得多”不太自然。
C准确表达regret to say和for good；A可能像去世，B不够自然。
A/C/D/E准确；B“老实人”含义略偏。
A等准确自然；C“去掉”搭配稍弱。
A准确自然；B/E保留英文名不宜，E只限长相；C/D暗示不像父亲过强。
정확하고 자연스러우며 '통로'가 secret path에 적절함
의미가 정확하고 자연스러운 표준 표현
'looked good'와 'moreover'를 자연스럽게 반영함
'to the effect that'를 '내용의 메모'로 정확하고 자연스럽게 옮김
'예정되어 있었다'가 planned for의 뜻에 가장 자연스러움
돕는 대상에 대한 높임과 전체 의미가 자연스럽게 전달됨
capable of doing을 '충분히 합격할 수 있는'으로 가장 명확히 반영함
should를 추측이 아니라 당위로 정확히 번역함
fear for my life를 간결하고 자연스럽게 표현함
'Give me a ring'의 관용적 의미를 자연스럽고 정중하게 번역함
slipped into의 '어느새 젖어 들다' 뉘앙스를 자연스럽게 살림
'among them'의 각자 한몫했다는 뉘앙스를 가장 잘 반영함
make up my mind를 자연스럽게 '결정을 못 했다'로 표현함
put up with noise의 상황을 가장 자연스러운 한국어로 전달함
fed up with complaining을 구어체로 매우 자연스럽게 표현함
look forward to를 '손꼽아 기다리다'로 자연스럽게 번역함
run out of luck을 '운도 다하다'로 자연스럽고 정확히 옮김
please의 정중함과 요청의 자연스러움이 가장 좋음
came across를 '우연히 마주쳤다'로 자연스럽게 번역하고 이름 표기도 적절함
far from stopping을 '멈추기는커녕'으로 정확하고 자연스럽게 표현함
I regret to say의 발화 태도를 가장 충실하게 반영함
As far as I know에 해당하는 가장 정석적이고 자연스러운 표현
bad habit is formed와 hard to get rid of를 자연스럽게 '습관이 들다/고치기 어렵다'로 표현함
take after를 '닮았다'로 정확히 옮기고 이름 표기도 자연스러움
B/C are exact; D/E also good but 'patika' better for path.
A/B/C accurately express leaving by train.
All are accurate; 'güzel görünüyordu' is most natural here.
B naturally conveys that the note said he was going out for lunch.
A is accurate and natural; D is slightly less idiomatic.
'Market poşetlerini' most naturally captures groceries being loaded into the car.
E best conveys being capable of succeeding on the test.
All are accurate; 'böyle' is a natural rendering of 'that' in context.
C is the most natural way to express fearing for one's life because of the words.
B correctly renders the idiom as 'call me'; A is missing.
C best captures gradually/unconsciously falling into a new way of life.
'El birliğiyle' naturally captures 'among them' as collective responsibility.
All are accurate; A is direct and natural.
All are accurate; B is very natural with 'çok fazla gürültü'.
A best conveys being fed up with the ongoing complaining.
A/B/E correctly use present expectation; C/D suggest past expectation.
All are accurate; 'eninde sonunda' is especially idiomatic for sooner or later.
All are natural; B is a clear neutral request.
All are accurate; 'karşılaştı' is the most general natural equivalent.
C most idiomatically renders 'far from stopping'.
E naturally conveys regret and that he has gone permanently.
All are accurate; C explicitly includes 'he' and 'man'.
All are accurate and natural.
All are accurate; 'annesine çekmiş' idiomatically renders 'takes after his mother'.
A and B are identical and excellent. C uses 通路 (passage/corridor) which is slightly less natural for an outdoor path. D and E omit 側 which is minor but A/B are most complete.
A, B, C, E are identical and correct. D has a typo (出発しましました) making it malformed.
A has an error: かなりに is unnatural/wrong for 'looked good'. C and D are both natural and accurate; C slightly more precise with 見た目がよかった and 適正. D is equally strong.

B is concise and natural using 旨 alone without redundant という. C has redundant という旨 which is slightly awkward. D mistranslates lunch as 給食 (school lunch). A and E are correct but slightly more verbose.

D correctly uses 来週の土曜日 which is the most natural rendering of 'next Saturday'. B mistranslates 'originally' as まず第一に and changes meaning. A, C, E use 次の土曜日 which is acceptable but slightly less natural than 来週の土曜日.
A uses 青年 matching 'young man' precisely and お年寄りの女性 is natural. D is also excellent with 老婦人. C is awkward with 買った食料 and 積むことを手伝った structure.

A and D are both excellent. A uses 落ちる which is the natural colloquial term for failing a test. B completely mistranslates as 'ability test'. C and E use 失敗する which is slightly less idiomatic for test failure.
A is natural and accurate. B changes 'most' to 大多数 and uses こう instead of そう, slightly altering meaning. C is equally good. D uses たいていの which is acceptable but slightly less precise than ほとんど.

A naturally conveys the meaning with 身の危険 and adds 聞いて for naturalness. D is equally good. C mistranslates as 'I become afraid of dying' which misses the 'fear for my life' nuance. B and E are good but slightly less natural.

A and C both naturally render the idiom 'give me a ring'. B changes to 'I'll be waiting for your call' which alters the imperative. C is equally natural and casual. A is slightly more polite and balanced.
A, B, and E all excellently capture 'slipped into' with いつの間にか/自然と and 馴染んでいった. C uses 入っていきました which is less idiomatic for 'slip into'. D is too literal and loses the gradual/natural nuance.

B, C, E all use 寄ってたかって which perfectly captures 'among them' as a collective action. A uses みんなで which is weaker and loses the conspiratorial nuance. D uses 結託して (conspired) which implies more deliberate scheming than the original.

A uses 決めかねています which precisely captures 'haven't made up my mind' (still in the process of deciding). C is equally good but more casual. B and E use 決めていません which is slightly less nuanced. D mixes polite and casual registers.
C is complete and natural with proper subject inclusion. B omits 私たちは but is still natural. A has awkward word order with はずい分. E uses ひどい which slightly overstates 'a lot of'.
A and B are both excellent. 不平 and 愚痴 both work well for 'complaining'. A's もううんざりです is natural. C omits もう which weakens the 'fed up' feeling. D adds 不満 unnecessarily and uses きみたち.

A, C, D, E are all excellent and nearly identical. B uses present tense 心待ちにしている which doesn't match the present perfect 'have been looking forward to'. A is chosen as representative of the best group.
A and B are both excellent. B's も adds a nuance of 'even he' which is a slight addition not in the original. C and E use でしょう which is slightly softer than だろう but acceptable. D is also good.
A, C, D, E are identical and excellent. B is too casual and omits 音量 making it less precise, though understandable.

A and E are both excellent. E uses ばったり which vividly captures the chance encounter. A is clean and natural. D uses the English 'Jack' in Roman letters which is inconsistent. B and C are good but slightly less vivid.
A, B, D, E are all excellent. C changes word order putting やむどころか first which is slightly less natural. A is chosen as representative.

A best captures both 'I regret to say' and 'gone for good' naturally. B is accurate but plain. C is overly verbose with 言わざるを得ません. D and E use 永遠に去った which is accurate but slightly more dramatic than the original.

B, C, D are identical and excellent using 私の知る限り which is the most natural rendering. A uses 私の知っている限りでは which is slightly verbose. E uses 誠実 (sincere) instead of 正直 (honest) which is a slight meaning shift.
B is very natural and idiomatic with なかなか抜けません. D is also excellent. A and C use 直す which is slightly more about correcting than breaking a habit. E is good but slightly verbose.
B, C, E are all excellent. A uses Roman letters for Peter which is inconsistent. D is incomplete/malformed (父より母にである makes no sense).
密道 is the most natural and idiomatic term for a secret path; the others are accurate but slightly verbose.
我们是坐火车走的 uses 走 which naturally echoes 'left/departed' and sounds most colloquial and idiomatic.
D uses 看着 and 挺合适 which sound most natural and colloquial; C's semicolon is awkward in Chinese.
A best captures 'to the effect that' with 大意是说 and keeps the tense natural; B omits 大意 losing the nuance.
原计划 is the most concise and natural phrasing for planned schedules in Chinese; all others are fine but slightly wordy.
C uses 老奶奶 (warmer, natural) and 买的东西 (natural for groceries); A and E keep 食品杂货/杂货 which is less natural in spoken Chinese.
A is idiomatic and natural, capturing the rhetorical/incredulous tone well with 明明会做 and 考砸了; C and D are overly literal.
A, B, D, E are identical and excellent; C omits 都 which slightly weakens the universality. Picking A as representative winner.
C captures the natural spoken register and emotional weight most vividly; others are accurate but more formal/flat.
A adds 吧 which conveys the casual/friendly request tone of 'give me a ring'; others are slightly more abrupt.
A's 悄然融入 best captures the gradual, unnoticed quality of 'slipped into'; B loses the subtlety with 慢慢适应.
A best captures 'among them' (collectively/conspiring) with 合起伙来; C and D lose the collaborative nuance.
C combines 稍等 (polite) with 拿定主意 (idiomatic for make up one's mind), making it the most natural and complete translation.
C and E are both excellent; C uses 不得不 and 很多噪音 naturally. A uses 得 which is slightly weaker for 'have to'.
All translations are identical and excellent. A selected as representative winner.
A, C, D are equally natural and idiomatic with 盼着他来; B and E are slightly more formal. A selected as representative.
C and E naturally make 好运 the subject, which sounds more idiomatic in Chinese; A, B, D are grammatically awkward.
调低 is more standard for volume (turn down = lower); 一点 adds natural softness to the request. C is the most natural.
B, C, E all accurately convey 'came across' as an accidental encounter; D uses the English name Jack untransliterated which is inconsistent. B selected as representative.
B is the most elegant and idiomatic with 停歇 and 愈演愈烈, a natural Chinese four-character expression perfectly fitting the context.
C adds 告诉你 which naturally reflects the speech-act of 'I regret to say' directed at a listener, making it most contextually complete.
老实人 is a more natural and idiomatic Chinese expression for an honest person in everyday speech compared to the more literal 诚实的人.
A, B, D are all excellent and identical; C uses 坏毛病 and 去掉 which are slightly less standard. A selected as representative winner.
A is natural and accurate; D is also good. B mixes English name with Chinese awkwardly and has unnatural structure; E keeps English name inconsistently.
A uses casual register which is natural for this context; '통로' is more precise than '길' for 'path/secret passage'. B, D, E are identical polite forms, also fine.
B, C, E are all natural and accurate. A is slightly more formal (습니다) but correct. D drops '는' subject marker awkwardly. B is chosen as natural polite form.
B and E are identical and best capture 'looked good' with '좋아 보였고' and 'moreover' with '게다가'. C is natural but omits the 'looked' nuance. A uses 마음에 들었고 which shifts meaning slightly.
B and E both accurately render 'to the effect that' as '내용의' and use natural phrasing. D uses '취지의' which is slightly formal/legal. A is casual and accurate but drops the subject.
C adds '그' (the) which matches the English 'the meeting', uses '예정되어 있었어요' naturally, and is polite without being overly formal. D and E are also good but omit '그'.
E is natural, uses '젊은이' (young man), '할머니' (culturally appropriate for old lady), '도와드렸어요' (respectful helping), and smooth word order. B has redundant '젊은 청년'. C uses '노부인' which sounds stiff.
D captures the rhetorical/questioning nature well with '충분히 합격할 수 있는' and polite form. B is also good but '떨어져?' is very casual. A adds '어떡해요' which changes the meaning.
'Should' here expresses expectation/likelihood, not obligation. A and E correctly use '생각할 거예요'. C and D mistranslate 'should' as obligation ('해야 해').
B naturally conveys 'make me fear for my life' with '두려움을 느끼게 해'. C is also good. A and E use '생명의 위협이 느껴지네요' which is slightly off ('threat' vs 'fear for'). D is casual and natural.
'Give me a ring' is an idiom for 'call me'. C and D both render it naturally as '전화해 줘' in casual register. A and E are polite but slightly more formal than the casual idiom suggests.
A and B both excellently capture 'slipped into' with '어느새 젖어들었습니다/어요'. '어느새' conveys the gradual, unnoticed nature of 'slipped into'. E omits '어느새'.
'Among them' means collectively/together. E's '합세해서' (joining together) captures this well. D's '합심해서' is also good. B's '저마다 한몫해서' is acceptable. A's '어쩌다 보니' misses the collective meaning.
All are accurate. A uses '결정을 못 했어요' which is slightly more natural and direct. B and C use '마음을 정하지 못했어요' which is also natural. E's '마음을 못 정했어요' is equally fine.
A accurately conveys 'a lot of noise' with '시끄러운 소리를 많이' and is natural. B has awkward word order with '우리는' placed oddly. C softens 'a lot' too much. E's '심한 소음' changes the nuance slightly.
B is the most natural and idiomatic rendering of 'fed up with your complaining' using '진짜 지긋지긋해'. A and E are polite and good. C's '진저리가 납니다' is stiff. D drops the 'we' subject.
A best captures 'looking forward to' with '손꼽아 기다려 왔습니다' including the present perfect aspect '왔습니다'. D is also good but drops the subject. C uses '기대하고' which is weaker.
B uses '머지않아' (sooner or later/before long) and '운이 바닥날' which is vivid and natural. '바닥나다' (run out) directly mirrors 'run out of luck'. Others use '다할' which is slightly less idiomatic.
A uses '음량' (volume/sound level) which is precise. D adds '좀' making it more natural/polite. E uses '소리' which is colloquially natural. All are good; A is slightly more precise.
B and E both use Korean name '잭' and natural phrasing. B uses '마주쳤어요' (ran into) which captures 'came across' well. C and D are also accurate. A keeps English name which is less learner-friendly.

A uses '그치기는커녕' which is natural for storms (그치다 = stop/cease for weather). B, D, E use '멈추기는커녕' which is also correct. C adds '기미는커녕' which is slightly awkward. A is most idiomatic for weather context.
A naturally renders 'I regret to say' as '유감스럽게도' and 'gone for good' as '영영 떠나버렸어요'. The '버렸어요' adds the sense of finality. B adds unnecessary honorific '그분'. E is overly literal.
A and E both use '제가 알기로는' which is natural. B and C use '아는 한' which is also correct. A uses formal '입니다' matching the slightly formal English. All are good; A is chosen for precision.
E is natural and concise: '나쁜 습관은 한번 들면 고치기 어려워요'. Uses '고치다' (fix/correct) which is idiomatic for habits. All options are reasonable; E balances naturalness and accuracy best.

B uses Korean name '피터', natural '닮았어요', and polite register. E is identical in quality. A and C keep English name. D uses casual '아빠/엄마' which is fine but slightly too informal for a neutral statement.
A is completely wrong (sleeping like a baby). B and C are identical and best: 'patika' (path/trail) is more precise than 'yol' (road/way).
A/B/C are identical and most natural. D and E are acceptable alternatives but slightly less direct.
'güzel görünüyordu' is more natural than 'iyi görünüyordu' for 'looked good'. B/D/E are identical and best. C lacks semicolon matching the original punctuation.

B uses 'öğle yemeğine çıkacağını belirten' which is the most natural rendering. C and D use past tense incorrectly ('çıktığına'/'çıktım'). A and E use 'dair' which is slightly more formal but acceptable.

All are good. D uses 'planlanmıştı' and 'önümüzdeki cumartesiye' which is natural. E's 'İlk başta' is slightly more colloquial. All are essentially equivalent; D is slightly more idiomatic with the dative case.
D uses 'market poşetleri' (grocery bags) which most precisely matches 'groceries' as physical items being loaded. Others use 'alışveriş' (shopping) which is slightly abstract for loading into a car.

E uses 'başarabileceğin' (capable of passing/succeeding) which best captures the meaning of 'capable of doing' in the context of a test. Others use 'yapabileceğin' (capable of doing) which is acceptable but less idiomatic.
A/C/D/E use 'böyle' (like this/such) which is more natural. B uses 'öyle' which is slightly less natural in this context. All are essentially equivalent; A is fine.

E is the most natural: 'beni hayatım için endişelendiriyor' directly conveys 'make me fear for my life'. D is also good. A and B use awkward reflexive constructions ('endişe etmeme/duymama neden oluyor'). C drops the causative structure.
A is null/missing. B/C/D/E all correctly translate the idiom 'give me a ring' as 'beni ara' (call me).

'slip into' implies a gradual, almost effortless transition. D's 'geçiverdi' captures the sudden/easy aspect with the '-iver' suffix. A adds 'sessiz sedasız' (quietly) which is an interpretation. C and E are acceptable.
'Among them' here means 'between them/together they managed to'. B and E use 'el birliğiyle' (in cooperation) which best captures this idiomatic meaning. A and D use 'aralarında' too literally.

A and C are identical and excellent. 'Henüz kararımı vermedim' is the most natural. B's 'karar veremedim' implies inability rather than not yet deciding. E uses 'bir saniye' which is fine but less common.
B/D/E use 'çok fazla gürültü' which better matches 'a lot of noise'. A and C use just 'çok gürültü' which is slightly less emphatic. B/D/E are identical; B wins.

A adds 'sürekli' (constantly) which captures the ongoing nature of complaining implied by 'your complaining', and 'artık' adds natural emphasis. B lacks 'artık'. D and E use 'şikayetlerinden' (complaints) which is slightly less natural than the gerund form.
'I've been looking forward to' is present perfect continuous, so present tense 'bekliyorum' is correct. C and D use past tense 'bekliyordum' which is wrong. A/B/E are identical and correct.
'Eninde sonunda' is the most idiomatic Turkish equivalent of 'sooner or later'. D and E are identical and best. A/B/C use 'er ya da geç' which is a more literal translation.
A uses informal imperative 'kıs' with 'lütfen' after, which is very natural. B and E are also excellent. C and D use formal 'kısın' which is fine but slightly more formal than needed.
'Rastlamak' (to come across/encounter by chance) is slightly more idiomatic for 'came across' than 'karşılaşmak'. A/D/E are identical and best.

A/D/E use 'dinmek bir yana' (let alone stopping/calming) which is very natural for storms. C uses 'şöyle dursun' which is also idiomatic. B uses 'durmak' which is less natural for storms. A/C/D/E are all excellent.
B and D both capture 'I regret to say' well. A is too brief and loses 'I regret to say'. C is overly verbose. E is good but B is slightly more natural with 'ki'.
A is most concise and natural, dropping the redundant 'o' (he). B/C/D/E are all good but slightly more verbose.
All translations are essentially identical and excellent. 'Bir kez' and 'bir kere' are both correct. A wins arbitrarily.
A/D/E use 'çekmiş' which is the idiomatic Turkish for 'takes after' (resembles in character/appearance). B uses 'benziyor' which is more literal. C has awkward word order.
